Q. X was a niece of Rabindranath Tagore and among the first women to graduate from Calcutta University, winning the Padmavati Gold Medal in 1890. She is credited with setting "Vande Mataram" to music. In 1910, she founded Bharat Stree Mahamandal in Allahabad - the first national-level women's organisation in India.
In 1919, Y visited Lahore for the first time and stayed at X's home while her husband was imprisoned for his role in the Rowlatt Satyagraha. A close friendship developed. Over the following months, the two exchanged letters at a feverish pace - at one point, Y sent 25 letters in 16 days. Y referred to their bond as a "spiritual marriage" and wrote to a friend: "Our relation is beyond definition." In one letter to X, Y confessed: "You still continue to haunt me even in my sleep."
The relationship eventually cooled, reportedly after intervention from C. Rajagopalachari. Years later, in 1936, Y told the American birth control advocate Margaret Sanger that he had once "nearly slipped" with a woman of "broad cultural education" but had been "saved" by those around him.
X and Y both passed away before seeing what fate had in store: X's only son married the daughter of Y's cousin.
ID X and Y.
